tests.mutation: In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.Eligible ignored the willingness statement (`if (false && !willing.Willing)`), so an unwilling creature reached the anatomy decline instead of being refused; this test went red and no other did. It went red too when "at least one size larger" counted the rider's own size as larger (`steps < 0` for `steps < 1`).

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.AppropriateAnatomy read an unstated anatomy as appropriate (`if (false && anatomy.Verdict == AnatomyVerdict.NotStated)`), so this creature was a mount instead of declining; this test went red, and so did appropriate-anatomy's own decline test.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.Eligible ignored the GM's determination and asked the anatomy rule as though nothing were stated (`AppropriateAnatomy(AnatomyStatement.NotStated(candidate, anatomy.StatedBy))`), so a willing creature a size larger declined whatever the GM said; this test went red and no other did.
